newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Travel and tourism urged as part of WTO agenda.
newsitem.headline: Travel and tourism urged as part of WTO agenda.

text.p: Travel and tourism should feature as a full agenda item of the World Trade Organisation, Geoffrey Lipman, president of the World Travel and Tourism Council, said on Wednesday.

Lipman told a meeting of representatives of Singapore's travel and tourism industry that a full WTO place was needed because "travel and tourism will emerge as one of the three new paradigm service economic sectors of the 21st century, alongside telecommunications and information technology".

He told Reuters after the meeting that he had received a "positive response in general" to the idea from WTO officials, although he did not expect it to be on the agenda of the WTO ministerial meeting to be held in Singapore in December.
Lipman was in Singapore unveiling a new tourism council report on the island republic's booming travel sector and launching WTTC's "millennium vision".
That calls for making the sector an economic priority, opening world markets, sustaining development, and removing barriers to growth.

The Singapore report predicts travel and tourism in the island republic will grow 56 percent to S$41.8 billion (US$29.6 billion) annually by 2006, up from a projected S$19.1 billion in 1996, resulting in the creation of an estimated 41,000 jobs.
Lipman said Singapore would be "a great new tourism and transport dynamo" of the 21st century, growing faster than the world average of 49 percent over the period.
